main_concern: This is a design-review checkpoint with no completion claim, which is healthy. However, the central architectural decision—whether the RSP-02 fixed matrix fields live inline in intent_judge output or in a separate matrix-check command—is still unresolved. Until that decision is made with a written rationale and a migration path for existing hook consumers, the implementation could accidentally drift toward either (a) fields that hooks ignore, or (b) a second LLM-heavy gate that weakens the deterministic first line.
top_risks: Separation of the matrix from intent_judge creates a new surface that hook authors can forget to call, producing silent high-risk pass-through at UserPromptSubmit / PreToolUse.
Degraded / timeout handling for semantic review may silently demote a high-risk directive to answer_only unless the fallback rule is provably conservative and covered by negative samples.
Surface increase in LLM participation (more fields, more samples, more logging) could be mistaken for a safety improvement while the actual adjudication rule becomes less deterministic.
missing_evidence: Full current codex-hook.py showing exactly how UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse consume intent_judge today (bundle is truncated).
Current check_runner.py and runtime/bin/redcap showing how a new RSP-02 check would be registered in the regular regression suite.
A concrete proposed schema or diff for the five fixed RSP-02 matrix fields, not only the existing JUDGMENT_SCHEMA.
minimum_fix: Before editing runtime code: (1) decide inline-vs-separate matrix and record the decision with a consumer-compatibility rule; (2) write the conservative degraded/timeout fallback policy and at least one negative sample proving it blocks a high-risk directive when semantics fail; (3) list the six required sample categories and identify one canonical example per category.
